result.topic_en: Latin notes showing that the general solution of a linear heat-conduction-type equation consists of terms of the form $f(t)e^{\lambda t}$, with $f$ a polynomial in $t$, and analysing when $\lambda$ must be constant or may depend on the spatial variables; then reduction of the equation $\Delta u = du/dt$ to differential quotients with respect to one variable only.
result.transcription:
Solutionem generalem aequationis $\sum_\nu a_\nu \frac{\partial^\nu u}{\partial t^\nu}$ e terminis formae $f(t)\, e^{\lambda t}$ conflatam esse constat, denotante
$f(t)$ functionem integram ipsius $t$ et [-quantitatem $\lambda$-] quantitatem a $t$ non pendentem, facileque perspicitur
hos terminos singulos aequationi (I) satisfacere debere. Iam demonstrabimus, [-quantitates $\lambda$ esse constantes esse debere-] [-constantes esse-] [-terminis-] fieri non posse, ut sit $\lambda$ functio ipsarum $x_1, x_2, x_3$.
[-Sit-] Sit $k t^n$ terminus summus functionis $f(t)$ distinguanturque duo casus [-quando-]
1° [-Si-] $\lambda$ [-est realis aut-] {+est+} realis aut formae $\mu+\nu i$ et $\mu, \nu$ functiones unius functionis realis $\alpha$ ipsarum $x_1 x_2 x_3$; substituendo
{+Quando+} $u = f(t) e^{\lambda t}$ in [-aequatione I-] parte laeva aequationis I, coefficiens ipsius $t^{n+2} e^{\lambda t}$ invenitur $=$
$k \left(\frac{\partial \lambda}{\partial \alpha}\right)^2 \sum_{\iota,\iota'} a_{\iota,\iota'} \frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial x_\iota} \frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial x_{\iota'}}$. Sed haec quantitas evanescere nequit, nisi $\frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial x_1} = \frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial x_2} = \frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial x_3} = 0$ sive $\alpha = \text{const}$, quum
forma $\left( a_{\iota,\iota'} \quad \right)$
ut supra monuimus, sit forma positiva.

2°. Quando $\lambda$ est formae $\mu+\nu i$ et $\mu, \nu$ sunt functiones independentes ipsarum $x_1, x_2, x_3$, quantitates
$\mu+\nu i$ & $\mu-\nu i$ pro variabilibus independentibus $\alpha$ & $\beta$ sumi [-potest-] {+licet+} continebitque ipsum $u$
praeter terminum $f(t) e^{\lambda t}$ etiam terminum complexum conjugatum, [-qui sit-] $f_1(t) e^{\lambda_1 t}$.
[-Iam $\Delta u$ est-] Quodsi
$\Delta u = a\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \alpha^2} + b\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \alpha \partial \beta} + c\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \beta^2} + e\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha} + f\frac{\partial u}{\partial \beta}$
est, {+substituendo $u = f(t) e^{\lambda t}$+} [-invenitur-] {+et+} aequando coefficientem ipsius $t^k e^{\lambda t}$ cifrae, [-invenitur a=0-] [-obtinetur-] [-invenitur-] $a = 0$
[-ex aequatione $\Delta u = 0$-],
et perinde {+$b=0$+} substituendo $u = f_1(t) e^{\lambda_1 t}$. Unde ope aequationis $\Delta u = 0$ aequatio $\Delta u = \frac{du}{dt}$ ita trans-
formari potest, ut solos quotientes differentiales secundum alteram utram variabilem contineat.
Sed substituendo $u = f(t) e^{\lambda t}$, $u = f_1(t) e^{\lambda_1 t}$ coefficiens summi cujusque horum quotientium differen-
tialium invenitur $= 0$, unde et hi quotientes differentiales ex aequatione $\Delta u = \frac{du}{dt}$ [-evanescere-]
omnes excidere debent, q. e. d.
In casu igitur posteriore functio $u$ componitur e numero finito terminorum formae
$f(t) e^{\lambda t}$, in quibus [-$f(t)$-] $\lambda$ est constans et $f(t)$ functio integra [-ipsius-] $t$.

In casu priore quando habetur aequatio formae
[-—-] (1) $\sum_\nu a_\nu \frac{\partial^\nu u}{\partial \alpha^\nu} = 0$
[-expressio generalis ipsius-] functio $u$ erit formae
$u = \sum_\nu$ [-$\alpha$-] $q_\nu p_\nu$ [-$\alpha$-]
denotantibus $p_1, p_2, \ldots$ solutiones particulares aequationis (1) et $q_1, q_2, \ldots$ constantes arbitra-
rias sive functiones solarum $\beta$ & $t$. Quodsi haec expressio in aequationem
$\Delta u = \frac{du}{dt}$
substituitur, obtinetur aequatio formae
$\sum_i P_i Q_i = 0$
in qua quantitates $Q$ sunt quotientes differentiales ipsarum $q$ ideoque functiones solarum $\beta$ & $t$, quanti-
tates $P$ autem functiones solarum $\alpha$ & $\beta$. At talem aequationem supra vidimus, si ex $n$ terminis
constat, {+pro+} [?] {+subjicere+} praebere $\mu$ aequationes [-inter fun-] lineares inter functiones $Q$ & $n-\mu$ aequationes inter [-functio-]
nes $P$, quarum coefficientes sint functiones solius $\beta$, denotante $\mu$ [-numerum aliquem-] {+quempiam+} numerorum
$0, 1, \ldots, n$. Obtinebuntur igitur expressiones ipsarum $\frac{dq}{dt}$ per quotientes differentiales ipsarum
$q$ secundum $\beta$ ab ipsa $\alpha$ {+vacuo+} [?] liberae.

Iam casus singulos problematis nostri ad hunc casum pertinentes perlustremus.
{+Quando+} [-Si-] $m=2$ et $\Delta$ {+est+} formae $\partial_\beta^2 + e\,\partial_\alpha + f\,\partial_\beta$ aequatio reducta $\Delta u = 0$, si a quotientibus differentiali-
bus secundum $\beta$ libera evadit, [-erit formae-] formam induet
$\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial \alpha^3} + r\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \alpha^2} + s\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha} = 0$
unde $u$ erit formae
$ap + bq + c$

items.english: We shall now show that it cannot happen that λ is a function of x1, x2, x3.

items.english: In the latter case, therefore, the function u is composed of a finite number of terms of the form f(t)e^{λt}, in which λ is constant and f(t) is a polynomial in t.
